paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Mechanical Properties of TiAl Matrix Composites Reinforced with Different Types of High-Entropy Alloy Particles
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

evidence.quote: TiAl alloys are extensively utilized in aerospace and automotive applications, attributed to their superior properties.
TiAl matrix composites strengthened by high-entropy alloys (HEAs) using powder metallurgy techniques
This study investigates the effects of three high-entropy alloys (AlMnCrFeNi, CoMnCrFeNi, and CoMoCrFeNi) on the microstructure and high-temperature tensile properties of Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb composites.

the Ti4822 alloy is predominantly constituted by the lamellar a2-Ti3Al/c-TiAl structure and equiaxed c-TiAl phases
the Ti4822 alloy is predominantly constituted by the lamellar a2-Ti3Al/c-TiAl structure and equiaxed c-TiAl phases

numerous cavities existed in the Ti4822 alloy as displayed in Fig. 4(a). Such phenomenon implies that the deformation of Ti4822 powder is insufficient to acquire dense structure during the hot-pressing sintering process.
To the AlMn-HEA/Ti4822 composite, in addition to the two TiAl phases, diffraction peaks corresponding to the BCC structure are also observed.
independent HEA particles with sizes ranging from 30 to 120 lm display the dendritic cell-like morphology and are distributed uniformly throughout the matrix
Ultrafine HEA particles in both linear and punctate morphologies can be clearly observed surrounding the larger particles.
Similarly, in the CoMn-HEA/Ti4822 composite, diffraction peaks associated with the FCC phase are detected.
For CoMn-HEA/Ti4822 composite, beyond the c and a2 TiAl phases, CrMo phase (PDF#97-062-6310) and FCC phase introduced by the CoMn-HEA powder are also detected.
Additionally, a new TiCr2 phase also emerged.

attributes.location: interface between HEA particle and TiAl matrix

evidence.quote: The interface between the dendritic cell-like HEA particles and the TiAl matrix demonstrates robust bonding and the average thickness of the diffusion layer is approximately 22.39 lm.

the diffusion layer within the HEA particle shows a bilayer structure, which differs from the previous two samples. The average combined thickness of the inner and outer diffusion layers is ~22.37 lm.
